history.p: The present Passion oratorio, of which only an undated printed text book has survived, was performed by The Musical Society, presumably sometime between 1766 and 1773 when the society used the hall in Bryggernes Laugshus. The author of the text is the Norwegian writer and poet, Niels Krog Bredal, who moved to Copenhagen in 1770 when he became theatre director. Already in January 1760 he had written a 'Sørge-Oratorie' which, according to the newspaper Adresse-Contoirs Efterretninger, was performed in his rooms in Copenhagen. During 1761–70 he was mayor in Norway. It is likely that the present Passion oratorio was composed and performed after his arrival in Copenhagen in 1770. With the permission of Scheibe, Bredal might have used an early work of Scheibe's by simply replacing the original text with a new.

annot.p: '[...] Ligeledes blev i forige Uge paa Hr. Borgemester Bredals Værelser opført en deel af afgangne Medailleur Arbins Venner den over ham af bemeldte Hr. Bredal componerede Sørge-Oratorie'.

incipText.p: Saa faldt den hele Last af Syndens Straf paa dig
Ei Helved-Slangens List og Rænke
Det er fuldendt – det glade Budskab
Kierlighed vandt Seier
Din Kamp er ude – og jeg staaer tilbage
Det uvelkomne Skraal af Jøders Skare

incipText.p: O Himmel! – hvilken Skare af Mirakler!
Herefter skal da Død og Grav
Jeg ønsker kun med Længsel
Dertil hielp os Christus vor Trøst
Jeg knurrer ei mod din dybe Viisdom
Min Siæl er tændt af ædel Iver
Nu aabnedes mit Øye giennem Taarer
